name: Splenic Arteriovenous Malformation

criteria.description: Radiologic evidence of abnormal direct communication between splenic artery and vein on angiography or contrast-enhanced imaging
Presence of splenomegaly with associated symptoms such as abdominal pain or portal hypertension
Exclusion of other causes of splenic vascular anomalies or portal hypertension

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging confirmation of splenic arteriovenous communication plus clinical presentation consistent with splenic AVM
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily relies on imaging modalities; histopathology is rarely required.

laboratory: Cytopenias due to hypersplenism (anemia, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia)
Mild elevation of liver function tests if portal hypertension present
imaging: Contrast-enhanced CT or MRI showing early venous filling of splenic vein
Angiography demonstrating direct arteriovenous communication within spleen
Doppler ultrasound revealing turbulent flow and arterialized venous waveform
genetic: No known genetic mutations specifically associated
other: Physical exam may reveal continuous bruit over left upper quadrant
Histopathology rarely performed; shows abnormal vascular channels

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of direct arteriovenous shunting on imaging
Underlying liver disease with cirrhosis on imaging and labs
Absence of splenic arteriovenous malformation on angiography
History of trauma or iatrogenic injury
Focal lesion rather than congenital malformation

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe left upper quadrant pain indicating possible splenic rupture
Signs of high-output cardiac failure due to large AV shunt
Massive gastrointestinal bleeding from portal hypertension-related varices
